The fiscal freefall is real—debt hit 97% of GDP in 2023, barreling toward 200% by 2050 per GAO. Reconciliation’s a start, but let’s cut the theater. The 2017 tax cuts added $1.9T to deficits while HHS burned $2.9B on failed refugee contracts last March.

The Taxpayer Funds Oversight Act (H.R. 1558) finally forces CFOs to link performance metrics to spending, but Congress keeps rubber-stamping waste. Defense spending’s sacred, but why’s the Pentagon still failing audits?

Real fiscal health means torching bloat, not just shifting deck chairs. Until DC stops treating budgets like monopoly money, prosperity’s a pipe dream.

The House Ag GOP's farm bill proposal claims fiscal responsibility while boosting crop subsidies by $50B and relying on $53B in speculative CCC cuts. Reference price hikes for soybeans (19%) and cotton (13.5%) lock in corporate welfare for commodity giants, while the 10% marketing loan rate bump further distorts markets. SNAP "reforms" claw back $27B from nutrition to fund trade promotion doubling – classic Washington shell games.

This isn't fiscal discipline – it's robbing Peter (struggling families) to pay Paul (agribusiness). Real reform would sunset Depression-era subsidy programs entirely, not expand them. The 942-page monstrosity proves Congress still treats farmers like toddlers needing safety nets while actual rural priorities like broadband ($350M/year) get crumbs.

Until they slash the $15B/year crop insurance slush fund and means-test subsidies for mega-farms, this is just performative austerity.

The Fiscal Commission Act (H.R. 3289) proves Congress can tackle runaway deficits when structured correctly—mandating $1.6T in spending cuts while locking pro-growth tax policies. Arrington’s right: This model forces accountability by sunsetting bureaucratic bloat (Section 3(a)(2)(A)) and redirecting funds to strategic priorities like border security and energy dominance.

The CBO’s static $3.3T deficit projection ignores dynamic gains from deregulation and tariff revenue, which the Trump administration’s analysis shows could slash debt-to-GDP to 88% by 2039.

Real-world results? Wages up $7,200/year, 7M jobs protected. Washington’s finally prioritizing output over accounting tricks—a blueprint for sustained fiscal discipline.

Medicaid’s collapse isn’t about “stay-at-home sons”—it’s about systemic theft. Fraudulent enrollment, ER abuse by non-citizens, and bureaucratic bloat drain $55B annually in improper payments. Work requirements are a start, but real reform requires slashing redundant programs, enforcing eligibility audits, and ending state-level loopholes that prioritize non-citizens over taxpayers.

The One Big Beautiful Bill’s safeguards? Barely scratches the surface. Until D.C. stops subsidizing failure, Medicaid remains a sinking ship.

Fix the waste first—then talk about “commonsense.”
